summary: Tool rail is the vertical rail of tools from the Whiteboard template: Select and Pan, then Sticky note, Pen, Eraser, Shape, Connector and Text, then Comment, in three groups split by short lines. One tool is picked at a time. The picked tool sits on a soft accent tint (in Clean, its neutral selected fill), and each tool shows its name and its letter in a tooltip on hover.
use: When a board, a canvas or a drawing surface needs its tools within reach at the edge of the screen.
When people switch tools often and should always see which one is on.
When the tools fall into a few groups (moving round, making things, talking about them) that a line can split.
Not for actions that happen at once, like undo or zoom: Zoom bar holds those.
features: The nine tools are one radio group: a click picks a tool and unpicks the one before. The rail only shows the pick; what each tool does on your board is yours to wire up.
Each tool's tooltip shows its name and letter: V Select, H Pan, S Sticky note, P Pen, E Eraser, R Shape, A Connector, T Text, C Comment.
While the focus is in the rail, the arrow keys move the pick up and down it (wrapping at the ends) and a tool's letter picks that tool. The rail listens to no keys outside it.
Hover is the quiet row fill in the button's own shape, and a press shows at once as a deeper fill, with no scale.
The rail is Canvas toolbar's bar stood on its end: the same 32px buttons, the same raised pill with its shadow, square in Blueprint and plush squircles in Soft.
In React, `ToolRail` takes `value` or `defaultValue` and calls `onChange` with the tool's id (`select`, `hand`, `sticky`, `pen`, `eraser`, `shape`, `arrow`, `text` or `comment`).
a11y: The rail is a `toolbar` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, and the tools are a `radiogroup` of `radio` buttons, each with `aria-checked` and an `aria-label`.
Only the picked tool is in the tab order; the arrow keys reach the others, the way a radio group works.
The dividers are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader hears only the tools.

faq.q: How do I make the letters work anywhere on my board?
faq.a: Listen for the keys on your board and set the tool yourself: in React pass `value` and change it from your handler; in HTML click the tool's button (`.tlr-b[data-t="pen"]`) from yours. The rail answers its letters only while it has the focus.

faq.q: Can I lay it out across instead of down?
faq.a: The rail is drawn down the side, as on the Whiteboard. For tools across the bottom of a canvas, Canvas toolbar is the horizontal bar.

faq.q: Why does Clean show a grey fill on the picked tool?
faq.a: Clean keeps its controls monochrome: the picked tool takes its one neutral selected fill, where Soft and Blueprint use the accent tint.
